blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Hosea contests attribution of grain, wine, oil, fertility, and security to Baal or rival practices, but the text does not document one simple or uniform fertility cult. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. Interpretations differ on some details.

A literary feature to notice is that Hosea rhetorically reuses exodus, wilderness, Jacob, Gibeah, Baal-peor, and prophetic traditions to diagnose present identity and summon change. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.
